lines.text: Did you know that forests are not just silent trees, but an interconnected living biological internet?
Ecologists call it the Wood Wide Web, and it operates beneath your feet.
Trees connect their root tips to an expansive underground network of fungal threads called mycorrhizal fungi.
Through these fungal internet cables, older mother trees nourish shaded saplings with sugars and carbon.
When a tree is attacked by beetles, it sends chemical distress warning signals through the network.
Neighboring trees receive the warning and immediately ramp up protective tannins in their leaves.
A forest is not a competition; it is a collaborative superorganism.
